item.title: Jess Dillard-Wright
item.description: Jess is a white, fat, queer, genderqueer, feminist, antiracist, abolitionist, nurse dissident, activist-scholar. Dillard-Wright is associate professor and associate dean of equity and inclusion at the Elaine Marieb College of Nursing, University of Massachusetts Amherst, a Fellow of the American Academy of Nursing, and co-editor-in-chief of Nursing Philosophy. Her/their scholarship attends to ideas in nursing, working the intersections where feminism, nursing, and activism interact, from queer nursing histories and radical imagination to posthuman and new materialist care ethics. A founding member of the Nursology Theory Collective and co-organizer of Nursing Mutual Aid, she/they co-edited Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022) and remain a tentacle of the Compost Collaborative.

item.title: Jane Hopkins-Walsh
item.description: Jane is a white, bilingual, cis, hetero woman who works as a pediatric nurse practitioner in Boston, Massachusetts, USA. She holds a PhD from the Boston College Connell School of Nursing (2023) and completed a postdoctoral fellowship in nursing at Université Laval, Québec (2024–2025). In clinical practice at Boston Children’s Hospital Primary Care at Longwood since 1986, she is interested in the intersection of health and people in global mobility contexts. Her doctoral research examined patterning within stories about important people and events in the lives of emerging adults, ages 18–22, who have im/migrated from Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador. She co-edited Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022) and writes on critical posthumanist nursing.

item.title: Brandon Blaine Brown
item.description: Brandon is a white, cis, queer and newly middle class man. A registered nurse (MSN, RN-BC, CNL), he earned his B.S. in Nursing from Andrews University and a Master’s in Nursing Education from Norwich University. He is a Clinical Assistant Professor in the Department of Nursing at the University of Vermont, where he has taught since 2016, and practices in post-surgical and trauma care at the University of Vermont Medical Center, alongside doctoral study in education (EdD) at UVM. Brandon co-edited Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022) and writes at the intersection of nursing philosophy, posthumanism, and planetary health.

item.title: Eva Willis
item.description: Eva is white, cis, hetero woman from the countryside. A registered nurse and sociologist, she trained as a nurse in Germany and has practised in both German and British healthcare systems. She holds a BA in Social Sciences from the University of Kassel and an MSc in Sociology and Global Change from the University of Edinburgh. After a research post at Charité’s Institute of Clinical Nursing Science in Berlin, she is now a PhD candidate researching and teaching in the sociology of health and healthcare at the University of Siegen. Her PhD explores organisational knowledge embodied in nursing praxis and how the micropolitics of nursing affect patient care. Eva has two dogs and is committed to improving animal welfare.

item.title: Jamie B. Smith
item.description: Jamie B Smith is a white, cis, queer newly middle class man. He is a nurse, Senior Research Fellow at Edinburgh Napier University, and research associate at the Institute of Gender in Medicine, Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin, moving between research and clinical practice in the NHS. His Edinburgh PhD developed a posthuman institutional ethnography of nursing. His work explores how power, humans, and non-humans produce intimate relations and care in more-than-human worlds, combining critical posthuman theory and feminist new materialism with mixed methods research on nursing workforces, stress, and structural inequality. He serves on the editorial board of Nursing Philosophy.

item.title: Christian Tedjasukmana
item.description:
Christian Tedjasukmana (he/him) RN, BSN, MFA is a nurse, artist, and designer based in the USA. Christian melds nursing and art together; his work calls attention to current myopic healthcare practices that contribute to climate change and negatively impact health.

Selected works

  • Metastatic growth: The healthcare industry’s increasing contribution to the plasticene — in Nursing a Radical Imagination (Routledge, 2022)
  • Notes on [post]human nursing: What It MIGHT Be, What it is Not — Nursing Inquiry (2023)

item.title: Annie-Claude Laurin
item.description: Annie-Claude Laurin, Inf., Ph.D., is an Assistant Professor (professeure adjointe) in the Faculté des sciences infirmières at Université Laval, Québec, Canada, and a researcher at the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec. An intensive care nurse at the CHU de Québec–Université Laval since 2016, she completed her doctorate at Laval with SSHRC funding, studying nurses’ lived experience and actions in contexts of acharnement thérapeutique: perceived aggressive and futile treatment at the end of life in the intensive care unit. She is interested in the philosophical, social, and political structures which sustain this culture of death denial, in care and relational ethics, epistemic injustice, and nurses’ moral agency and resistance.

item.title: Patrick Martin
item.description:
Patrick Martin is a professor (professeur) in the Faculté des sciences infirmières at Université Laval, Québec, Canada. His work brings political philosophy into nursing: care ethics and democratic institutions, anarchism, epistemic injustice, and nurses’ resistance. He co-authored the collective’s imperative for critical posthuman research in nursing and appears in the Solidarity videos.

item.title: Kieran Sheehan
item.description:
Kieran Sheehan is an artist working with video. His piece for the collective, Constantly Becoming With (Yorkshire, UK, 2022), is a series of video wonderings — moving images that stay with entanglement, decay, and regrowth.

Photo and full bio to come — Kieran will fill this profile in his own words.
